newsitem.title: UK: IBC says trading good, eyes acquisitions.
newsitem.headline: IBC says trading good, eyes acquisitions.

text.p: IBC Group Plc said on Tuesday trading had been good in the first quarter of 1997 and that it was expecting to make further acquisitions this year.
"We've done well in the first three months of 1997 so we're encouraged by that. We've got good finances to support both acquisitions and organic growth," chief executive Peter Rigby told Reuters.
Finance director Tony Cropper said that the performance in the first quarter of 1997 had exceeded that of the same period of last year and was also ahead of budget.

IBC, which runs exhibitions and trade shows and publishes a range of business titles, reported a 10 percent rise in 1996 pre-tax profit to 13.7 million stg. Turnover was up 24 percent to 120.3 million.
IBC shares gained strongly after the results, adding 15p to 336p, their highest level for some 18 months.
Rigby said IBC had 30 million stg available for acquisitions, having recently arranged a 35 million facility with JP Morgan and Barclays Bank.
"We are looking very seriously at acquisitions,' said Rigby, saying these were likely to be in the publishing sphere.

He said that 1996 had been a "bedding down" year for IBC, noting the company had spent a modest 1.3 million stg on two acquisitions last year. But he said the company had spent some 15 million stg on a range of business titles in the previous 15 months.

IBC is active in a range of overseas markets, notably Germany, the Netherlands, Singapore and the United States. Finance director Cropper said the strength of the pound had shaved around 500,000 stg from profits last year.
But he said that he believed the company was strong enough to deliver growth this year despite the continuing strength of sterling.
IBC is active in a number of expanding market sectors such as telecommunications, pharmaceuticals and the legal world.
